columns.name: id
columns.description: The unique identifier for an entity. Read-only.

columns.name: appId
columns.description: The unique identifier for the application that is assigned by Microsoft Entra ID. Not nullable. Read-only. Alternate key. Supports $filter (eq).

columns.name: displayName
columns.description: The display name for the application. Maximum length is 256 characters. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values), $search, and $orderby.

columns.name: createdDateTime
columns.description: The date and time the application was registered. The DateTimeOffset type represents date and time information using ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC time. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014 is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z. Read-only.  Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, and eq on null values) and $orderby.

columns.name: signInAudience
columns.description: Specifies the Microsoft accounts that are supported for the current application. The possible values are: AzureADMyOrg (default), AzureADMultipleOrgs, AzureADandPersonalMicrosoftAccount, and PersonalMicrosoftAccount. See more in the table. The value of this object also limits the number of permissions an app can request. For more information, see Limits on requested permissions per app. The value for this property has implications on other app object properties. As a result, if you change this property, you may need to change other properties first. For more information, see Validation differences for signInAudience.Supports $filter (eq, ne, not).

columns.name: identifierUris
columns.description: Also known as App ID URI, this value is set when an application is used as a resource app. The identifierUris acts as the prefix for the scopes you reference in your API's code, and it must be globally unique across Microsoft Entra ID. For more information on valid identifierUris patterns and best practices, see Microsoft Entra application registration security best practices. Not nullable. Supports $filter (eq, ne, ge, le, startsWith).

columns.name: onPremisesPublishing
columns.description: Represents the set of properties required for configuring Application Proxy for this application. Configuring these properties allows you to publish your on-premises application for secure remote access.

columns.name: id
columns.description: The unique identifier for an entity. Read-only.

columns.name: displayName
columns.description: The name displayed in the address book for the user. This value is usually the combination of the user's first name, middle initial, and last name. This property is required when a user is created, and it cannot be cleared during updates. Maximum length is 256 characters. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values), $orderby, and $search.

columns.name: userPrincipalName
columns.description: The user principal name (UPN) of the user. The UPN is an Internet-style sign-in name for the user based on the Internet standard RFC 822. By convention, this should map to the user's email name. The general format is alias@domain, where the domain must be present in the tenant's verified domain collection. This property is required when a user is created. The verified domains for the tenant can be accessed from the verifiedDomains property of organization.NOTE: This property can't contain accent characters. Only the following characters are allowed A - Z, a - z, 0 - 9, ' . - _ ! # ^ ~. For the complete list of allowed characters, see username policies. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, endsWith) and $orderby. This property is subject to sensitive action restrictions; only specific privileged administrator roles can update it.

columns.name: accountEnabled
columns.description: true if the account is enabled; otherwise, false. This property is required when creating the object. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, and in). This property is subject to sensitive action restrictions; only specific privileged administrator roles can update it.

columns.name: createdDateTime
columns.description: The date and time the user was created in ISO 8601 format and UTC. The value cannot be modified and is automatically populated when the entity is created. Nullable. For on-premises users, the value represents when they were first created in Microsoft Entra ID. Property is null for some users created before June 2018 and on-premises users synced to Microsoft Entra ID before June 2018. Read-only. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , ge, le, in).

columns.name: id
columns.description: The unique identifier for an entity. Read-only.

columns.name: appId
columns.description: The unique identifier for the associated application (its appId property). Alternate key. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, in, startsWith).

columns.name: displayName
columns.description: The display name for the service principal. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values), $search, and $orderby.

columns.name: accountEnabled
columns.description: true if the service principal account is enabled; otherwise, false. If set to false, then no users are able to sign in to this app, even if they're assigned to it. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, in).

columns.name: id
columns.description: The unique identifier for an entity. Read-only.

columns.name: displayName
columns.description: The display name for the group. Required. Maximum length is 256 characters. Returned by default. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values), $search, and $orderby.

columns.name: securityEnabled
columns.description: Specifies whether the group is a security group. Required.Returned by default. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, in).

columns.name: createdDateTime
columns.description: Timestamp of when the group was created. The value can't be modified and is automatically populated when the group is created. The Timestamp type represents date and time information using ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014 is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z. Returned by default. Read-only.

columns.name: id
columns.description: The unique identifier for an entity. Read-only.

columns.name: createdDateTime
columns.description: The date and time the sign-in was initiated. The Timestamp type is always in UTC time. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014 is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z.  Supports $orderby, $filter (eq, le, and ge).

columns.name: userPrincipalName
columns.description: User principal name of the user that initiated the sign-in. This value is always in lowercase. For guest users whose values in the user object typically contain #EXT# before the domain part, this property stores the value in both lowercase and the 'true' format. For example, while the user object stores AdeleVance_fabrikam.com#EXT#@contoso.com, the sign-in logs store adelevance@fabrikam.com. Supports $filter (eq, startsWith).

columns.name: appDisplayName
columns.description: The application name displayed in the Microsoft Entra admin center.  Supports $filter (eq, startsWith).

columns.name: ipAddress
columns.description: The IP address of the client from where the sign-in occurred.  Supports $filter (eq, startsWith).

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: alternateUrl
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: If you're configuring a traffic manager in front of multiple app proxy applications, this user-friendly URL points to the traffic manager.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: applicationServerTimeout
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: The duration the connector waits for a response from the backend application before closing the connection. Possible values are default, long. When set to default, the backend application timeout has a length of 85 seconds. When set to long, the backend timeout is increased to 180 seconds. Use long if your server takes more than 85 seconds to respond to requests or if you are unable to access the application and the error status is 'Backend Timeout'. Default value is default.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: applicationType
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: System-defined value that indicates whether this application is an application proxy configured application. The possible values are quickaccessapp and nonwebapp. Read-only.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: externalAuthenticationType
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Details the pre-authentication setting for the application. Pre-authentication enforces that users must authenticate before accessing the app. Pass through doesn't require authentication. The possible values are: passthru, aadPreAuthentication.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: externalUrl
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: The published external URL for the application. For example, https://intranet-contoso.msappproxy.net/.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: internalUrl
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: The internal url of the application. For example, https://intranet/.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: isAccessibleViaZTNAClient
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates whether the application is accessible via a Global Secure Access client on a managed device.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: isBackendCertificateValidationEnabled
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates whether backend SSL certificate validation is enabled for the application. For all new Application Proxy apps, the property is set to true by default. For all existing apps, the property is set to false.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: isContinuousAccessEvaluationEnabled
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates whether continuous access evaluation is enabled for Application Proxy application. For all Application Proxy apps, the property is set to true by default.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: isDeviceAccessEnabled
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates whether the Microsoft Entra Private Access application is accessible or available in device access mode. false by default.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: isDnsResolutionEnabled
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates Microsoft Entra Private Access should handle DNS resolution. false by default.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: isHttpOnlyCookieEnabled
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates if the HTTPOnly cookie flag should be set in the HTTP response headers. Set this value to true to have Application Proxy cookies include the HTTPOnly flag in the HTTP response headers. If using Remote Desktop Services, set this value to False. Default value is false.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: isOnPremPublishingEnabled
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates if the application is currently being published via Application Proxy or not. This is preset by the system. Read-only.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: isPersistentCookieEnabled
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates if the Persistent cookie flag should be set in the HTTP response headers. Keep this value set to false. Only use this setting for applications that can't share cookies between processes. For more information about cookie settings, see Cookie settings for accessing on-premises applications in Microsoft Entra ID. Default value is false.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: isSecureCookieEnabled
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates if the Secure cookie flag should be set in the HTTP response headers. Set this value to true to transmit cookies over a secure channel such as an encrypted HTTPS request. Default value is true.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: isStateSessionEnabled
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates whether validation of the state parameter when the client uses the OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant flow is enabled. This setting allows admins to specify whether they want to enable CSRF protection for their apps.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: isTranslateHostHeaderEnabled
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates if the application should translate urls in the response headers. Keep this value as true unless your application required the original host header in the authentication request. Default value is true.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: isTranslateLinksInBodyEnabled
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates if the application should translate urls in the application body. Keep this value as false unless you have hardcoded HTML links to other on-premises applications and don't use custom domains. For more information, see Link translation with Application Proxy. Default value is false.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: onPremisesApplicationSegments
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Represents the application segment collection for an on-premises wildcard application. This property is deprecated and will stop returning data on June 1, 2023. Use segmentsConfiguration instead.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: segmentsConfiguration
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Represents the collection of application segments for an on-premises wildcard application that's published through Microsoft Entra application proxy.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: singleSignOnSettings
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Represents the single sign-on configuration for the on-premises application.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: trafficRoutingMethod
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates how traffic is distributed across multiple connectors in a connector group. The possible values are: none, random, sessionPersistence, performance (Not implemented), unknownFutureValue.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: useAlternateUrlForTranslationAndRedirect
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Indicates whether the application should use alternateUrl instead of externalUrl.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: verifiedCustomDomainCertificatesMetadata
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: Details of the certificate associated with the application when a custom domain is in use. null when using the default domain. Read-only.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: verifiedCustomDomainKeyCredential
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: The associated key credential for the custom domain used.

microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.name: verifiedCustomDomainPasswordCredential
microsoft.graph.onPremisesPublishing.description: The associated password credential for the custom domain used.
